exercises.title: Write Enqueue and Dequeue
exercises.task: Fill Enqueue (refuse when full) and Dequeue (refuse when empty). The only arithmetic is where the back is, and moving head with wrap-around.
hints: The back slot is head + count, wrapped: (r.head + r.count) % len(r.buf).
Dequeue takes r.buf[r.head], then moves head one step, wrapped the same way.
Without %, the indices run past the end of the array after the first lap.

exercises.title: Time-sharing, round robin
exercises.task: In 1961 a time-sharing system let one computer serve several people at once: each program runs for at most quantum units, then goes to the back of the queue if it is not finished. Return the names of the programs in the order they finish. (The names are commands of CTSS, the MIT system of 1961.)
hints: A slice works as a queue here: take q[0], then q = q[1:]; append unfinished programs at the back.
A program that needs exactly quantum finishes in its turn: it does not go back in the queue.
